stem:
Diya places samples on a hard surface and beats each with a hammer. An iron strip flattens into a thinner sheet. A lump of coal breaks into pieces.

Which claim about these samples is correct?

options.text: Iron is malleable because it flattens; coal is brittle because it breaks.
Iron is neither malleable nor brittle.
Coal is malleable because it changes shape when beaten.
Both samples are brittle because a hammer was used on each.

teacher.key_rationale: Flattening into a sheet shows malleability; breaking into pieces shows brittleness. Iron flattens; coal breaks.
